fields.title: Nothing checks that a .NET build collects coverage

sections.What it checks:
* [std-NETTST.coverage-is-collected-by-the-build] says a build "**MUST** collect coverage from its test run and publish
  the report".
* It says a build "**SHOULD** collect it with `dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"`, which writes a Cobertura
  report".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The check this rule needs is a pipeline step after `dotnet test`. It fails where the run wrote no Cobertura report:

```sh
find . -path '*/TestResults/*/coverage.cobertura.xml' | grep -q .
```

A build using another collector, as the `SHOULD` allows, changes the path the step searches for.

The step has to come from a shared pipeline template that branch policy requires. A team writing its own pipeline leaves out the step along with the collector. A pre-commit check or a Claude Code hook sees the pipeline definition, and could only search it for the collector flag.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the pipeline definition is the only thing that notices a missing collector today.

The check proves a report was written. It does not prove the report was published, or that each test project is excluded from its own figure.
